Right — when converting from header to module, the names that were previously inside `namespace geo { ... }` in the header are now exported into the global namespace at the module level (since I put `export` directly on each declaration without wrapping them in `namespace geo {}`). So `TriangleArea` is at the global scope, not `geo::TriangleArea`.

The task said: "put `export` directly on each declaration individually (`export struct Vec2`, `export Vec2 Add(...)`, `export double Cross(...)`) — do NOT wrap them in a `export namespace geo { ... }` block instead." So the declarations are at the global scope. `app.cpp` must call them without the `geo::` prefix. The task also said "Leave main() unchanged" for app.cpp — but that conflicts with the requirement that declarations are no longer in the `geo` namespace.

Reading the spec carefully: "`export struct Vec2`, `export Vec2 Add(...)`, `export double Cross(...)`" — this is just an example pattern showing the `export` keyword directly. The instruction "do NOT wrap them in a single `export namespace geo { ... }` block instead" means: don't use a wrapping export-block, use individual exports. But that doesn't necessarily mean the namespace has to disappear.

I think the most natural reading that satisfies *all* constraints is: keep the `namespace geo { ... }` block (as it was in the original .cpp), and put `export` on each declaration individually inside that namespace. The "do NOT wrap" rule means don't add a new wrapper — the existing `namespace geo { ... }` is just normal code. The spec gives the `export struct Vec2` *form* as an example but the underlying intent is "no new wrapping `export namespace` block."
